title: Moss-stitch scarf
subtitle: A dense, reversible fabric with a two-row bump texture.
excerpt: A flat scarf worked in UK moss stitch (a two-row alternating knit-purl pattern) on 4.5 mm needles with DK yarn, finishing at 20 cm wide and 175 cm long. The two-row repeat produces larger, rounder bumps than seed stitch.
sourceNotes: UK double moss stitch (sometimes called Irish moss stitch) is documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938) and throughout Weldon's Practical Knitter as a standard textured fabric stitch. Note: UK moss stitch and US moss stitch describe different fabric structures; this pattern uses the UK double-row pattern (K1,P1 / K1,P1 / P1,K1 / P1,K1).
heroPrompt: A moss-stitch scarf in forest green DK wool, showing the characteristic two-row bump texture, with the scarf loosely rolled to reveal the fabric on both sides.

knitting.gaugeText: 20 sts x 30 rows = 10 x 10 cm in moss stitch on 4.5 mm needles, blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A UK knitting stitch pattern worked over an even stitch count in a four-row repeat: rows 1 and 2 work K1, P1 across; rows 3 and 4 work P1, K1 across. This produces rounded, clearly defined bumps larger than seed stitch. Called double moss stitch in some UK sources to distinguish it from the US moss stitch pattern.
A cast-on method using the tail and working yarn together to form an elastic, neat edge.

content.text: This is a flat scarf worked from one short end to the other in
moss stitch (UK double moss)

on 4.5 mm needles with DK yarn, finishing at 20 cm wide and 175 cm long. The two-row repeat produces a more pronounced bump than seed stitch and reads as a dense, cushiony fabric that lies flat and looks the same on both sides.

Flat construction is the natural choice for moss stitch: the fabric is self-stabilising and needs no border. The two-row repeat means you must track whether you are on a Row 1/2 pass or a Row 3/4 pass. Using a row counter or making a small mark when the pattern shifts helps. The finished scarf uses about 165 g (375 m / 410 yards) of DK-weight yarn.
What you need

items.name: DK-weight wool or wool-blend yarn
items.substitutions: Any DK yarn. Solid and semi-solid colours show the texture best.

content.text: Gauge

20 sts x 30 rows = 10 x 10 cm in moss stitch on 4.5 mm needles, blocked. Each stitch off gauge changes the finished width by about 1 cm; each two rows off gauge across the full 525-row scarf adds or removes about 7 cm of finished length.
Stitches used
K (knit), P (purl). In UK moss stitch, you work the same stitch for two rows before switching: two rows of K1,P1 across, then two rows of P1,K1 across.
Pattern
Cast on
Use the
long-tail cast-on
to place 40 stitches. Tail length: (14.1 x 40) / 10 + 15 = about 71 cm.
Stitch count check-in: 40 stitches after the cast-on.
Body
Rows 1 and 2: (K1, P1) to end. (40 sts)
Rows 3 and 4: (P1, K1) to end. (40 sts)
Repeat these four rows until the scarf measures 175 cm from the cast-on edge. This takes approximately 525 rows. At the halfway mark (about 87 cm), count: still 40 stitches.
Cast off
Cast off in pattern on a Row 1 or Row 3 of the repeat. Work at normal tension; moss stitch does not pull in at the cast-off as rib does.
Common faults

Pattern reverting to seed stitch (single-row repeat instead of double). This happens when the row count is lost and the stitches are swapped every row instead of every two rows. Use a row counter and mark each time you complete two rows of the same sequence.
Broken columns or vertical streaks. Usually caused by working a K1,P1 row when the pattern calls for P1,K1, or vice versa after a distraction. Read the stitch on the needle to check what comes next.
Extra stitches. Yarn left in front before a knit stitch at the start of a new row adds an unintended yarn-over. Check the yarn position every time a row starts with a knit.
Finishing
Weave in ends. For wool, wet blocking will even the stitches: soak, press out water, and lay flat to dry.
Care
Handwash wool in cool water and lay flat to dry. For cotton and acrylic, follow the yarn label.
What to try next
The basketweave scarf arranges knit and purl squares into a grid pattern, using the same two stitches in a more structured block repeat.
